QF.id: Role of RTAs in Mutual Fund Transactions_9

question.text: Which of the following tasks is handled by the RTA in relation to depository operations?

answer.text: Setting the NAV for demat units differently from physical units
Acting as the depository for holding mutual fund units in electronic form
Approving new demat account openings for mutual fund investors
Providing the depository interface and processing conversion of mutual fund units between physical and demat form

explanation.text: The Logic: RTAs provide the depository interface for mutual funds and process the conversion of physical mutual fund units to demat form and demat units back to physical form (remat), acting on behalf of the AMC. The Trap: The RTA is not the depository itself - NSDL and CDSL are the depositories. The RTA interfaces with them as the AMC's agent. NAV is uniform across forms of holding, and DPs (not RTAs) open demat accounts for investors. Note: Investors initiate demat or remat of mutual fund units through their DP or the ISC, and the RTA carries out the conversion in coordination with the depository.
